jobs.description:
The Department of Physics and Astronomy (IFA), Aarhus University, Denmark (www.phys.au.dk) invites applications for a 2-year research assistant position with focus on establishing and maintaining trapped ion quantum technology setups. The work will partly be carried out in the newly established Quantum Tech-nology Lab (QTL) and within the Ion Trap Group.

The position is open from 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. 

Your profile
The candidates are expected to have experience in cold trapped ion research, and hence both have experience in ion trap and laser technology. We are seeking enthusiastic candidates with a keen interest in setting up a new teaching ion trap setup in QTL as well as participate in maintaining and running ion trap experiments within the Ion Trap Group. More specifically, the candidate should have a solid background in construction and operating rf ion traps, CW laser systems including control of output powers, polarization states, linewidths and frequencies, as well as an understanding of analog and digital electronics for experimental control. Relevant methodology includes UHV vacuum handling, rf circuity electronics, laser frequency stabilization using optical frequency combs, rubidium atomic clocks, and GPS synchronization.

Applicants must be able to document relevant experience, as outlined above.

Who we are / The department
The Department of Physics and Astronomy is a department at the Faculty of Natural Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark. The main objectives of the Department are to carry out research at the highest interna-tional level, to offer research based teaching at Bachelor of Science, Master of Science and PhD levels, and to exchange knowledge with other areas of society, e.g. by offering our expertise to industrial partners and the business world.

The Department is an attractive workplace for researchers, teachers, technicians, laboratory technicians and administrators and has a good study environment with many talented and active students at all levels. The research at the Department of Physics and Astronomy is of high quality, attracts significant international attention – in several fields the Department is within the world elite – and is characterized by many international collaborations with other high-ranking universities and research institutions around the world.

The place of work is Ny Munkegade 120, 8000 Aarhus C and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

The successful candidate is offered
• a working climate inviting lively, open and constructive discussion within and across different fields of research
• a working environment with teamwork, close working relations, and social activities
• a workplace characterized by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance
• a job where the overall environment in Denmark is family-friendly, safe and relaxed – contributing to Denmark consistently being voted amongst the happiest nations in the world.
 
Job description
Your tasks include:

• Establishing and running a novel linear rf ion trap setup for teaching purposes
• Handling existing CW laser systems including commercial external cavity diode laser systems, TiSa-lasers, fiber-lasers for trapped ion experiments
• Handling (electro-)optical setups for controlling the frequency and shaping the power level of CW laser
• Help developing experimental control systems based on the platform ARTIQ (ARTIQ)

Contact information
Further information can be obtained from Michael Drewsen (drewsen@phys.au.dk)

Deadline
The application deadline is 13 December 2026. 

Application procedure
Short-listing is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

About Aarhus University

Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. The university offers an inspiring research and teaching environment for its 37,500 students, including PhD students, and has 9,000 employees (full-time equivalents) and an annual revenue of EUR 1.2 billion. Learn more at international.au.dk

We are looking for an engineer who wants to build the foundation of our new Integrations effort: the connectors that bring our customers' data from third-party systems into the Trackunit platform. The connectors you build directly support our new partnership business, one of our key goals for next year. You will be among the first developers on this project, designing a reusable architecture and working directly with the engineers behind the systems we connect to, as well as seeing customer feedback shape what you build next. You might have a couple of years or be an experienced senior engineer, either way, we would be interested in seeing your application for this role.

**What's in it for you?

**

• Shape how the work gets done. Join a new, small team set up next to an established platform team, and help define how integrations get built here.

• Hear directly from the people using what you build. Customer feedback feeds straight back into the roadmap, and we act on it quickly.

• Collaborate beyond your own codebase. You’ll have regular, technically focused conversations with developers from the systems we connect to.

• Learn from experts who share. You’ll work with experienced domain experts who are open to sharing what they know, so you learn quickly.

• See your work ship. We favour small, frequent releases over long project cycles, so progress is visible fast.

**Who are you ideally?

**You are a backend developer with strong Java skills, just as comfortable at the edges where systems meet as inside your own codebase.

• Strong hands-on experience with Java, Spring Boot, Kafka, and REST APIs, in particular consuming data from other systems, in a microservice architecture.

• Experience designing new, reliable, reusable architecture for integrating with multiple systems. System-to-system integration experience is what we value most.

• You are comfortable discussing technical feasibility and approaches with third-party technical teams.

• You care what happens when data moves between systems, so you build with quality, observability and reliability in mind and you know quickly when something breaks.

• You are motivated by incremental delivery, enjoy getting close to the data, and like building new foundations from scratch.

You embrace AI as part of how you engineer. From prototyping through to production, you use AI tools as an integrated part of your workflow, not as a shortcut but as a force multiplier. That said, this isn't the main thing we're hiring for: curiosity and a willingness to use it well matter more than deep prior experience.

Don't meet every single requirement? No worries, this is what we're looking for ideally. If you're excited about this role but your background doesn't align perfectly with every point above, we encourage you to apply.

**Primary Responsibilities

**

• Design a reusable architecture for integrating with multiple third-party systems, not one-off solutions.

• Build connectors that collect data from third-party systems, usually ERPs, mainly by consuming their REST APIs, and bring it reliably into our platform.

• Understand the data you collect and transform it into Trackunit's data model.

• Work with third-party vendors: discuss technical feasibility and approaches with their technical counterparts.

• Build with quality, observability and reliability in mind, on our microservice and event-driven architecture.

****Our hiring process

****Don’t waste your time writing the perfect cover letter. We want you to create an impact that matters - and that’s not in the cover letter.

• Initial phone conversation with a colleague from our P&T team.

• Virtual meet and greet with your potential new leader and someone from the team, so you’ll get to know the role and team better.

• Assignment-specific interview with the hiring manager and a lead engineer from the team. We want to give you a real insight into the work. You’ll receive a case to prepare ahead of the interview and present to relevant colleagues - people you’ll also work closely with in the role.

• If needed, we will obtain references from former employers and conduct background checks at relevant levels.

• Offer presentation and walk-through.

**Coming Together To Connect Construction

**We’re committed to construction - one of the largest industries in the world. Over the past two decades, Trackunit has been pioneering technological progress within construction. Today, we are not only a leading IoT provider but a thought leader, supporting and shaping the agenda for an entire industry on a global scale.

We believe in taking a people approach in everything we do. Being human-centric is not restricted to our products - it’s a way of life at Trackunit. We’re proud to be a truly global team. Our colleagues come together in hubs spread across the globe, but we embrace the idea of working remotely and in environments that inspire you. Everything we do, we do to eliminate downtime and build the most useful industry for the world.

The question is: Are you in?

People & Organization

**Bring structure, service and ownership to every step of the employee journey

**Are you a detail-oriented P&O professional who enjoys working with people, processes and systems? Join Xellia’s Copenhagen P&O team for a one-year interim assignment and help deliver high-quality support across the entire employee lifecycle – from hire to retire.

Working close to the business

You will join a small, collaborative P&O & Payroll team in Copenhagen, supporting our Danish and Norwegian organisations and working with international colleagues. With four colleagues in the local team and approximately 18 across global P&O, you will have varied responsibilities, direct contact with employees and managers, and the opportunity to contribute to improvements in how we work.

Your role – make things happen

You will provide reliable day-to-day P&O administration and practical support across the hire-to-retire process, including:

• Prepare employment contracts, addendums and other documentation; keep employee and payroll-related data accurate and up to date.

• Support recruitment activities, including interviews, assessments and candidate feedback, and help organise onboarding and introduction days.

• Manage employee changes and offboarding in P&O, payroll, time and leave systems; respond to questions from employees and managers.

• Support annual P&O processes, including bonus and salary review cycles and administration linked to collective agreements.

• Maintain P&O policies, templates, digital personnel records and approval workflows, supporting compliance and audit readiness.

• Prepare P&O and payroll-related data for internal and external stakeholders and share relevant updates with leaders.

• Contribute to ad hoc P&O projects, including opportunities to simplify and automate processes using digital tools and AI.

What you bring

• A strong administrative background, ideally with experience in P&O or a similar people-support function.

• Strong working knowledge of P&O administration, employee documentation and digital HR/payroll systems, with the ability to use tools accurately and consistently.

• Ability to coordinate multiple hire-to-retire processes, maintain reliable data and deliver timely, high-quality outcomes.

• A service-minded approach to supporting managers and employees, with care, accuracy and follow-through.

• Clear communication skills in Danish and English, both written and spoken.

You take accountability for your commitments and adapt readily when priorities change. You combine practical functional knowledge with confidence in P&O systems and tools, and you work well with colleagues and stakeholders from different cultures and backgrounds. You listen to the needs of managers and employees and take pride in providing reliable support.

A word from our team

“Great P&O support is about more than processes and administration. It’s about understanding people’s needs, taking ownership and making everyday work easier for our colleagues. We are looking for someone who enjoys bringing structure, quality and a service-minded approach to everything they do — and who wants to be part of a team where we support each other and make a real difference.”

Kira Mondrup, Director, Global Employee Relations and P&O Copenhagen

What’s in it for you?

• Xellia isn’t for all: There’s no rigid hierarchy here, and no one will micromanage you. You’re trusted — and expected — to take real responsibility, perform at a high level, and learn fast. In return, you get the opportunity to shape how things are done, influence decisions, and make a visible impact.

• Make things happen: You’ll step into an organization in motion, with clear direction and ambitious goals. Here, you can grow fast, take on more than a fixed role, and shape what’s next alongside people who want to win.

Are you interested?

We would like our new colleague to join as soon as possible.

We are your people

Everything we do connects to our purpose to save lives. Every day, every task we do plays a part in one of the biggest battles of our time: fighting the most powerful bacteria on the planet. But at Xellia, it's not just about what we do - it's about how we do it and who we do it with. We work side by side, eye to eye, and heart to heart across functions and sites, building strong relationships and making an impact. We run on curiosity, trust, and honest conversations. We speak up and share what we know. It's not just where you want to go. It's who you get there with. At Xellia, we're your people.

Xellia is owned by Novo Holdings A/S, headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, and operates four sites globally.

Xellia Pharmaceuticals is the global leader in fermentation-based, non-beta-lactam anti-infectives, supplying Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) and Finished Dosage Forms (FDFs) to over 500 pharmaceutical companies across 80 countries.

Recognized by the World Health Organization and the European Union for our critical medicines, we play a vital role in combating severe infections and antimicrobial resistance. Headquartered in Denmark, we operate manufacturing sites in Copenhagen, Denmark; Budapest, Hungary; and Taizhou, China, with R&D and commercial operations in seven additional locations globally. As the only European manufacturer of several key anti-infectives and with a heritage spanning over 120 years, we are driven by purpose and progress.

With more than 1100 employees, our impact starts from within. We offer a workplace where ideas, curiosity, and initiative thrive, and where your role evolves with your ambition. Instead of rigid structures, we provide real responsibility, freedom to explore, and support to grow. Together, we shape not only the future of our company and the development of our people, but also the health of communities worldwide.

Further information aboutXellia can be found at: www.xellia.com

**Build software at scale. Influence how we build it. Help shape the next generation of development at Dalux.

**Dalux is growing, and we are looking for experienced software developers who want significant technical ownership while continuing to build software hands-on.

You will work on products used by professionals around the world, contribute to architectural and technical decisions, and help us improve how we develop software – including how we use agentic AI to make capable developers more effective.

**Your role

**As an Experienced Software Developer, you will take ownership of complex product and technical problems from idea to production.

You will work in a product team with other developers, a Product Manager, and a Product Designer. We expect experienced developers to contribute beyond their individual tasks by making good technical decisions, improving our architecture and development practices, and sharing knowledge with others.

Your work can include:

• Owning complex features and technical problems end-to-end

• Designing scalable, maintainable solutions and contributing to architectural decisions

• Improving our codebase, tooling, developer workflows, and technical quality

• Driving or contributing to initiatives around DevOps, CI/CD, infrastructure, architecture, or developer tooling

• Sparring with and mentoring other developers

• Working closely with Product Management and Design to understand problems and find the right solutions

• Bringing new ideas and technologies into Dalux when they can improve our products or how we build them

We expect experienced developers to have opinions, challenge existing solutions, and be comfortable having their own ideas challenged in return.

**Developing software with agentic AI

**We are significantly increasing our use of agentic AI in software development.

We use and explore AI across the development lifecycle – from understanding problems and navigating codebases to implementation, testing, debugging, refactoring, and review.

We are looking for developers who already use agentic AI as part of their development workflow. The specific tools matter less than how you use them: providing the right context and direction, critically evaluating the output, and knowing when to intervene or take a different approach.

Strong engineering fundamentals remain essential. AI can increase what a capable developer can achieve, but you remain responsible for the architecture, correctness, maintainability, and quality of the software you build.

At Dalux, you will help us take these ways of working further by experimenting, sharing what works, and helping establish effective practices for agentic software development.

**Technologies we work with

**Our platform is built on a distributed cloud architecture using AWS. Our primary technologies include:

• C# / .NET

• Angular / TypeScript

• GitHub Copilot

• MSSQL

• Elasticsearch

• AWS

• Optionally, Android / iOS development using .NET MAUI

You may also encounter parts of our C++ codebase.

Experience with our exact technology stack is useful, but strong software engineering fundamentals and the ability to understand and improve complex systems matter more.

**Product development at Dalux

**Our developers do more than implement specifications.

Developers, Product Managers, and Product Designers work together to understand problems and find solutions that balance user value, usability, technical feasibility, business viability, and long-term technical health.

Our products are relied upon by professionals worldwide, making performance, stability, maintainability, and quality important parts of everyday engineering.

**Your background

**We expect that you:

• Have solid professional software development experience

• Have at least six months of practical experience using agentic AI as part of your software development workflow

• Hold a university degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, IT, or a related technical field

• Have strong software engineering fundamentals

• Are comfortable owning complex technical problems and decisions

• Can navigate and improve an established codebase and architecture

• Care about maintainability, reliability, performance, and quality

• Enjoy technical sparring and sharing knowledge with other developers

• Understand the trade-offs between short-term delivery and long-term technical quality

Experience with C#/.NET, Angular, or cloud development is useful, but we do not expect you to match every technology we use.

**What You Can Expect From Dalux

**Dalux is a software company at heart. As an experienced developer, you can expect:

• Significant ownership and real influence on technical solutions

• Skilled colleagues who enjoy technical discussion and constructive challenge

• Close collaboration between Engineering, Product Management, and Design

• Short paths from ideas to decisions and implementation

• Opportunities to improve engineering practices beyond your immediate product work

• An environment actively investing in agentic AI for software development

• High levels of trust and freedom in how you solve problems

All Dalux software development takes place in-house at our headquarters in Vibenshuset, Copenhagen. Working together in person is an important part of how we collaborate, share knowledge, and make decisions quickly.

**About Dalux

**Dalux is a Danish software company founded in 2005 by Bent Dalgaard and Torben Dalgaard.

We build digital tools that make the construction industry smarter and more efficient. Using our own 3D BIM technology, we develop software used in more than 140 countries worldwide.

Our core technology is developed entirely in-house, giving our developers the opportunity to influence both the products and the technology behind them.

**Interested?

**If you want significant technical ownership while helping shape how modern software is developed at Dalux, we would like to hear from you.

**If agentic AI is already part of how you develop software, tell us how you use it – what you delegate, how you validate the result, and where you have found it genuinely useful.

**We recruit continuously and hire multiple experienced developers throughout the year as Dalux grows.

If you have questions about the position, contact IT Talent Acquisition Specialist Sara Nielsen on SNI@dalux.com

**Ongoing

Some of the most critical applications in Danish banking run on technology that predates modern engineering practices. In the Reduce Legacy Tribe, you will help change that — applying AI, automation and thoughtful architecture to make modernisation faster, safer and repeatable. This is engineering work with real consequences, and you will see the results.

What you will be doing

You will join a collaborative squad working across teams to modernise business-critical web applications serving advisors, business customers and private customers. This is a practical software architecture role, not an Enterprise Architecture position.

You will analyse codebases, design migration patterns and develop reusable tooling with engineers, translating technical understanding into architecture decisions that guide day-to-day work. Working closely with development and delivery teams, you will shape solutions, discuss trade-offs and resolve implementation questions to make migration approaches workable.

Development teams retain ownership of implementation and delivery; your role is to help them turn complex modernisation challenges into practical solutions.

More specifically, you will:

• Analyse legacy code, dependencies and business flows to choose realistic migration strategies

• Design gradual replacements and rebuild where direct migration would carry complexity forward

• Develop reusable migration patterns, transition designs and developer tooling with teams

• Explore AI agents for analysis, component generation, testing and migration verification

• Reduce lead time through automated quality checks and safer, smaller deployments

About you

• Practical software engineering background, for example as a software architect, lead engineer or senior software engineer

• Strong understanding of end-to-end application design, including frontends, APIs, security, testing and observability

• Ability to read and understand an existing codebase and assess when to migrate, simplify or rebuild

• Clear communicator who can summarise complex topics and discuss trade-offs with engineers

• Understanding of AI-assisted development: how to guide agents, assess generated code and validate results

Experience with legacy modernisation, reusable migration tooling or our stack (React, .NET BFF services, Kubernetes, mainframe integration and GitHub Actions) is a plus. Comparable technologies are equally relevant, and we value the perspective you bring from different environments.

What we offer you

You will work primarily from our Aarhus or Copenhagen office, with the flexibility to work from home up to two days per week. You will tackle difficult engineering problems with visible results on applications used by thousands of customers, working alongside engineers who are genuinely curious about what AI can do for modernisation.

There is real room to grow your architectural thinking and broaden your experience with emerging development practices.

Are you ready for the next step?

If you are ready to take on complex engineering challenges and help shape the path forward for critical banking applications, we would be glad to hear from you. Reach out to hiring manager Ole Bang Fredsø Weigelt at owei@danskebank.dk if you have any questions.

We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible or by 1 December 2026 at the latest.

We look forward to hearing from you!

Fixed income markets move fast, and clear, well-grounded analysis makes a real difference to the decisions clients and colleagues rely on every day. As a Fixed Income Strategist in our Fixed Income and FX Research team in Copenhagen, you will help shape the views we share with corporate and institutional clients across Europe. This is a role for someone with genuine curiosity and a commercial mindset.

What you will be doing

You will be part of a collaborative research team that works closely with Macro Research colleagues and strategists across our hubs. The team produces analysis that feeds directly into client decisions, and you will be a close sparring partner for both corporate and institutional clients. The atmosphere is open and collegial, with a shared commitment to rigorous, well-communicated research.

More specifically, you will:

• Produce interest rate forecasts and develop well-reasoned trading ideas

• Provide hedging recommendations to corporate and institutional clients

• Contribute to daily commentary on market developments and trends

• Represent our market views in client meetings and media appearances

• Collaborate with Macro Research and strategists across our hubs

Do you want to help keep the operational technology behind our wind assets reliable, resilient and ready for the future? We’re looking for an OT O&M Manager for Infrastructure to lead the services that enable secure connectivity, monitoring, control and operational data exchange across Business Area Wind.

OT infrastructure is the operational backbone of Business Area Wind. Every asset relies on it for secure connectivity, monitoring, control and the exchange of operational data.

We are looking for an OT O&M (Operation and Maintenance) Manager for Infrastructure within the OT team in Business Area Wind. This is an operational management role with end-to-end accountability for the performance, availability, reliability and continuous improvement of this business-critical service area.

You do not need to be the technical expert in every infrastructure domain. You do, however, need a strong understanding of OT environments and the ability to lead technical teams, challenge and support specialists, set priorities, make decisions and ensure that issues are driven through to resolution.

For this role, leadership, Accountability and Proactivity are as important as technical understanding. You will create the structure and momentum needed to deliver a reliable OT service.

The OT Infrastructure service area is responsible for the operation and maintenance of Operational Technology, including the hardware and software infrastructure that enables the flow of data between our enterprise network and our fleet of onshore and offshore wind farms. This includes central server infrastructure, such as asset data concentrators, data backup and restore solutions, and the supporting communication backbone, including Edge-to-Wide-Area connectivity solutions.

Be in your element with BA Wind

As part of BA Wind you will play a key role in one of the most exciting pipelines in the industry with 24GW of capacity stretching out more than a decade ahead across our key European markets.

You won’t only be involved in developing projects but pioneering cutting-edge innovation, new business models and ways of working with communities and the environment. Working as part of a leading European utility also means you could be helping a growing number of major businesses and brands achieve their own sustainability goals through partnerships.

Qualifications

Your role

You will take end-to-end ownership of the OT Infrastructure service area and ensure that the hardware, software and connectivity supporting Business Area Wind’s assets remain reliable, resilient and available. You will set priorities for the service area, lead and develop technical teams, and establish clear governance for performance, costs, risks and lifecycle needs. A central part of the role is to shape the service strategy and roadmap while ensuring incidents, recurring problems and improvement needs are identified early and driven through to sustainable resolution. Working across OT, Operations, IT, Cybersecurity, Engineering, Procurement, projects and suppliers, you will coordinate the expertise needed to manage critical operational dependencies and keep the service fit for future business requirements.

Your Tasks And Responsibilities

• Take end-to-end accountability for the OT Infrastructure service area, including its performance, availability, reliability, cost and continuous improvement.

• Lead and develop the service area teams, setting clear priorities and expectations while empowering technical specialists to deliver within their areas of expertise.

• Drive operational performance, ensuring risks, incidents, recurring problems and improvement needs are proactively identified, prioritised and followed through to resolution.

• Own the service strategy and roadmap, including priorities, budget, resources, lifecycle needs and service development in line with Business Area Wind’s operational requirements.

• Provide effective operational governance, using service performance, risks, KPIs and technical input to make decisions and ensure clear accountability.

• Manage stakeholders and interfaces across Business Area Wind, bringing together OT, Operations, IT, Cybersecurity, Engineering, Procurement, projects and suppliers to solve problems and deliver results.

• Ensure effective management of critical incidents and operational risks, providing leadership and escalation when required and ensuring lessons learned result in sustainable improvements.

• Drive continuous improvement, challenging existing ways of working where necessary and ensuring the service remains reliable, resilient and fit for the future.

Your profile

You combine a good understanding of OT infrastructure and operations with leadership experience from complex operational settings. You are comfortable taking Accountability for a business-critical service without needing to be the deepest technical expert in every infrastructure domain. Instead, you create clarity, set priorities and empower specialists to deliver, while remaining able to challenge recommendations and make informed decisions. With Proactivity, Collaboration, Composure and a Solution-Oriented approach, you provide direction during incidents and periods of operational pressure, bring stakeholders together and ensure agreed actions are completed. You are motivated by improving reliability, resilience and ways of working over time.

Next To This You Bring

• Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in operational management, O&M, IT/OT service management, infrastructure operations, engineering management or asset management, preferably within energy or another asset-intensive industry.

• Strong service-management capabilities, including operational performance, incident and problem management, lifecycle planning, risk management and continuous improvement.

Our offer

Looking for a role where your superpowers can be leveraged to the maximum and with limitless opportunities for growth?

jobs.occupation: Postdoc of Environmental Economics and Management
jobs.description:
The position is tied to three interdisciplinary European projects, MOSAIC, INTERCEDE and the upcoming Wild2050 project, which combine environmental valuation, environmental policy, and land use planning. The position is open from March 1st, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter, and it is a two-year position.

  In MOSAIC, the role will be primarily one of coordination: the postdoc will liaise with the leads of project’s case studies and synthesise results across cases, with a focus on the uptake of land use policy instruments and comparison of methods. This requires strong communication, organizational skills, and the ability to work independently with multiple international research partners. In INTERCEDE, the work will involve analyses around the demand for forest ecosystem services, and in Wild2050 how demand for biodiversity conservation may change towards 2050. Across the projects, this research will require experience with quantitative methods including monetary and non-monetary valuation as well as cross-country analysis all in an interdisciplinary setting.

  The postdoc’s duties will include research in environmental economics and management, as well as contributing to project reporting. The position may also include teaching or other duties.

  Further information on the Department is linked at https://www.ku.dk/ifro/en. Inquiries about the position can be made to Professor Jette Bredahl Jacobsen jbj@ifro.ku.dk or by phone +45 35 33 17 46.

  Physical presence at IFRO is considered as a natural part of being an employee to contribute to a welcoming, socially pleasant, creative and innovative work environment. IFRO offers possibility for flexibility and working from home, but an employee is expected to regularly be present physically at IFRO.

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

  Terms of employment

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

  Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  The application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  When you will be affiliated with the University of Copenhagen or otherwise have access to their research, you may be required to undergo a background screening. The purpose is to protect the security and research integrity of the University of Copenhagen.

  Please include 

   	
• Curriculum vitae 	
• Diplomas (Master and PhD degree or equivalent) 	
• Research plan – description of current and future research plans 	
• Complete publication list 	
• Separate reprints of 3 particularly relevant papers   The deadline for applications is 14 December 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.

   After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee.

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Interviews will be held on January 26, 2027.

Data Platform Manager

Posting Start Date: 10/14/26

Gentofte, DNK, 2820,

**Data Platform Manager, Digital & IT

**

• Location: Lisbon, Portugal or Copenhagen, Denmark

Are you passionate about building high-performing teams and shaping modern data platforms that enable business growth? Do you enjoy bringing together people, technology, and business needs to deliver scalable data solutions? Then you might be the person we are looking for.

As our new Data Platform Manager, you will be part of the Digital & IT organization and play an important role in advancing our enterprise data and analytics capabilities. You will lead a distributed team of data engineers while working closely with business stakeholders, Enterprise Architects, and technology teams across multiple locations to deliver reliable, secure, and scalable data solutions. This is a great opportunity to influence technology decisions, develop people, and shape the future of our data platform in an international organization.

**What Your Day Will Look Like

**In this role, you will typically focus on:

• Leading, coaching, and developing a team of data engineers across multiple locations, fostering a culture of collaboration, ownership, and continuous learning.

• Guiding the development, operation, and continuous improvement of a secure, scalable, and reliable cloud data platform.

• Establishing and promoting data engineering standards and best practices covering development, testing, deployment, monitoring, and documentation.

• Partnering with business stakeholders, Enterprise Architects, and technology teams to translate business requirements into practical and scalable data solutions.

• Overseeing the design and delivery of data pipelines, data models, and integrations from core business systems, including SAP, into the enterprise data platform.

• Shaping the platform roadmap by identifying opportunities to simplify, modernize, optimize costs, and create long-term business value.

**What You'll Bring

**

• Experience leading a data engineering, analytics engineering, or data platform team.

• Strong hands-on data engineering experience, including designing and building scalable, production-grade data pipelines and modern data warehouse or lakehouse solutions.

• Experience working with cloud data platforms such as Microsoft Fabric, Databricks, or Snowflake, combined with strong SQL and Python skills.

• Strong leadership, coaching, stakeholder management, and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across technical and business functions.

• Solid understanding of data engineering practices including ETL/ELT, data integration, CI/CD, data quality, operational monitoring, and DevOps principles.

• Experience working with SAP data environments, such as SAP S/4HANA, ECC, BW/BW4HANA, Datasphere, Business Data Cloud (BDC), or SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC), would be considered an advantage.

Do you want to bridge the gap between a device and the customer using it? We are looking for an experienced Backend Software Engineer to help bring our IoT devices to life for construction customers: how they are configured, installed, verified and kept running. You join the Device Management team, work side by side with our firmware and hardware teams, and your work shows up in the telematics devices out in the field.

Bring our devices to life for customers. Your work covers the device lifecycle as well as building the internal tools our hardware and firmware teams use to debug them. It applies to new and existing devices, our own and third-party ones. You will build the backend that enables our devices' configuration, with AI as the core of how you develop.

**What's in it for you?

**

• See your impact. Your work shapes how devices reach the construction industry and how quickly customers can use them.

• Work close to the hardware. You design with the firmware team, whose building blocks you combine like Lego into new device configurations.

• Learn from experienced colleagues. You join a team with people who have 20+ years of experience and who are first movers on technology and AI.

• Work with AI every day. The team develops with Claude Code and Cursor, and you can contribute within your first weeks.

• Freedom and responsibility. The team has a lot of both, with an open door whenever you need input.

**Who are you ideally?

**You are a backend engineer who cares that what you build works for the people using it, finds the way to the goal yourself, and knows which people to ask along the way.

• Solid hands-on experience with Java, Spring Boot and GraphQL, including designing APIs and databases and the services around them.

• You are results-driven and self-driven: you unblock yourself, reach out to the right people early and follow your work through to delivery.

• You like to learn from the team and bring others along, and you can design a solution end to end, from database to service, and explain your choices to colleagues in firmware and across engineering.

• Domain knowledge can be learned. An IoT background, such as an understanding of protocols, is a plus, but we value learning speed more.

• Nice to have: Postgres (or another relational database), Kafka or other messaging, Cassandra, GitHub, and experience working with MCP tooling.

AI is the core of how our team builds software, including a shared AI development workflow. We expect you to use AI as your main development platform, or to be keen to. Hands-on experience with AI-first development is a big plus.

Don't meet every single requirement? No worries, this is what we're looking for ideally. If you're excited about this role but your background doesn't align perfectly with every point above, we encourage you to apply.

**Primary Responsibilities

**

• Build new device configurations for our device administration tool, designed together with the firmware team, including bulk configuration updates for customers.

• Develop the backend behind them: API extensions, GraphQL, database design and orchestration, Java services and Kafka topics.

• Take features from the first idea to a device in the field, in close collaboration with our firmware and hardware teams.

• Support the rest of the device lifecycle, including installation, verification and the internal tool our hardware and firmware teams use to debug devices.

• Help the team grow: share what you know, review each other's work and raise the bar together.
